channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Trump, Xi, and Putin Meet at APEC Summit, Issue Peace Declaration
item.description: Leaders of the US, China, and Russia held their first in-person trilateral meeting at the APEC summit in Shenzhen. Following the talks, a Declaration of Heads of State on Peace was released. The document outlines areas of minimal consensus, including UN reform and energy markets, rather than territorial exchanges or plans for conflict zones.

item.title: Uzbekistan Navigates Relations Between Major Powers
item.description: Uzbekistan aims to develop relations with Russia, China, the US, and Iran simultaneously, attracting investment and expanding cooperation. However, each power has its own interests in Central Asia, and closer ties with one may displease another. This has been evident in recent diplomatic exchanges and disputes, raising questions about the sustainability of Tashkent's multi-vector policy and its associated risks.

item.title: US Ambassador: Business Uncertainty Hinders American Investment in Kyrgyzstan
item.description: US Ambassador Leslie Vigenere stated that unpredictable government procedures and a lack of business transparency are obstacles to attracting American investment in Kyrgyzstan. He emphasized the importance of legal stability, predictable government decisions, and capital protection for foreign companies. Vigenere noted that potential partners assess the investment climate based on how the government interacts with existing businesses.

item.title: US Ambassador Leslie Vigenere Concludes Mission in Kyrgyzstan; Successor Appointed
item.description: US Ambassador Leslie Vigenere has completed his nearly four-year diplomatic mission in Kyrgyzstan. Steven Gillen has been appointed as his successor, presenting his credentials on November 21. Vigenere noted significant economic changes, increased American business interest, and cooperation prospects in transport and aviation, including developing Kyrgyzstan as a regional air hub.

item.title: Iran's IRGC Claims Two Oil Tankers Hit Mines and Exploded in Strait of Hormuz
item.description: Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) announced that two oil tankers were hit by naval mines and exploded while transiting the Strait of Hormuz. The IRGC stated the tankers were using unauthorized routes north of Qeshm Island. They warned shipowners and commercial companies that the Strait is under Iran's full control, and relying on CENTCOM commanders will lead to heavy losses.

item.title: US Ambassador: Sanctions on Banks and Crypto Harm Kyrgyzstan's Reputation and Investment
item.description: US Ambassador Leslie Vigenere warned that sanctions risks in Kyrgyzstan's banking and cryptocurrency sectors threaten the country's international reputation and foreign investment. He expressed concern over the financial sector and crypto operations, stating that using Kyrgyzstan's system to bypass sanctions creates reputational risks. While acknowledging some steps taken, he urged further action.

item.title: Tehran claims strikes on two US bases in Bahrain
item.description: Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) announced strikes on two US bases in Bahrain, Sheikh Isa and Al-Jufair, in retaliation for US actions. Bahrain's Civil Defense reported a fire at an industrial facility following the attack, with no initial casualties. The IRGC also released footage of a tanker being destroyed for violating transit routes.

item.title: Dozens Killed and Injured in Russian Strikes Across Ukraine on November 22
item.description: Russian strikes on several Ukrainian regions on November 22 resulted in dozens of casualties, targeting residential buildings, shops, and infrastructure. The most severe consequences were recorded in the Kyiv region, with over ten deaths reported in Dymer and Vyshneve.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Oil Production and Exports Over 10 Years: Trends and Revenue Changes
item.description: Over the past decade, Kazakhstan has more than doubled its oil export revenues, reaching $40 billion in 2025 from $19.3 billion in 2016. While export volumes increased by 22.7%, revenue growth was significantly higher, peaking at $46.9 billion in 2022.

item.title: North Kazakhstan Region's Life: Russian Traces, Kazakh Steppe, and Deserted Villages
item.description: The population of North Kazakhstan, a key agricultural region, has been declining for decades as youth move to larger cities, leaving villages empty. Efforts to resettle people from the south have yielded limited results. This report examines the current situation of residents in border areas with Russia and their connections to the neighboring country.

item.title: Two Oil Tankers Hit Mines Near Strait of Hormuz, Catch Fire
item.description: Two oil tankers that violated navigation rules caught fire after hitting naval mines east of the Strait of Hormuz, the Iranian Navy announced. The incident occurred on November 22, when the vessels entered a restricted area despite prior warnings and with their navigation systems turned off. Details on tanker names and crew status are not yet released.

item.title: Explosion at Russian Warship in Benghazi, Libya, Causes Fire
item.description: Several powerful explosions occurred at a naval base in Benghazi, Libya, on the night of November 22. Military sources suggest an airstrike on ammunition depots, while other reports indicate an accidental event. The Russian corvette 'Merkuriy' was damaged and caught fire, according to Naval News. Ten people were injured.

item.title: Kazakhstan to commission five new solar power plants by 2026
item.description: Kazakhstan plans to launch five new solar power plants with a total capacity of 92 MW by 2026. Three plants are already operational, with two more expected to start by year-end. The Ministry of Energy has not disclosed the owners of these projects, but investigations reveal diverse investors including Singaporean companies and local groups.

item.title: Dushanbe Police Arrest Man with 30 Packages of Crystal Methamphetamine
item.description: Dushanbe police have arrested a 28-year-old resident suspected of drug trafficking. Authorities found 30 packages of methamphetamine, totaling 124 grams, in a rented car used for distribution. A criminal case has been initiated against the suspect.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan: Flood defense channel nearing completion in Issyk-Kul region
item.description: Construction of a 2,040-meter flood defense channel in Temir village, Issyk-Kul region, is nearing completion. The Ministry of Emergency Situations reports that once finished, the channel will protect over 200 homes, local roads, and a 600-meter stretch of the Bishkek-Karakol highway from mudflows. The project also includes the construction of 11 internal bridges.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan conducts first live power line repair without customer outages
item.description: For the first time, Kyrgyzstan has replaced porcelain insulators on power poles without cutting electricity supply. The repair was conducted on 0.4 kV lines in Bishkek's Birimdik residential area. This innovation allows for maintenance without disrupting power to consumers. The national grid company plans extensive repairs and reconstructions in 2026.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Can Attract Over $500 Million in Investments, Report Suggests
item.description: Kyrgyzstan has the potential to attract up to $618 million in private investment across fruit cultivation, processing, tourism, garment manufacturing, and fish farming. The Ministry of Economy and Commerce stated this could create up to 67,600 new jobs. A World Bank Group report identified barriers and proposed reforms.

item.title: New Production Facilities and Infrastructure Projects Launched Across Kazakhstan Regions
item.description: In the past week, Kazakhstan has seen the launch of new industrial, social, and infrastructure projects. This includes gas cylinder and valve production in Kokshetau, road repairs in Kostanay, and an IT lyceum in Taraz, as reported by the government's press service.

item.title: Kazakhstan: 45 Million Tenge Embezzled for Unrepaired Road
item.description: In the Pavlodar region of Kazakhstan, 45 million tenge allocated for intra-village road repairs have been embezzled. Prosecutors discovered that the Akimat of Uspensky rural district illegally transferred the funds to a construction company for an unrepaired road section. A criminal case has been initiated.

item.title: COP31 Climate Summit in Turkey Ends Without Agreement on Fossil Fuels
item.description: The COP31 climate conference in Antalya, Turkey, concluded without a consensus among over 190 participating nations on phasing out fossil fuels. Deep disagreements over the wording regarding the global transition away from fossil fuels and increased financial support for climate-vulnerable countries prevented the adoption of the Antalya Pact. The EU and other nations rejected proposals that did not explicitly mention fossil fuels.

item.title: COP31 Climate Summit in Turkey Concludes Without Political Agreement
item.description: The COP31 climate summit in Turkey concluded on Sunday without a comprehensive political agreement on addressing climate change. UN Secretary-General António Guterres expressed disappointment, noting the scientific consensus remains clear despite the lack of governmental action. China's Vice Minister Li Gao also voiced regret, stating that developing countries' demands were unmet.

item.title: Turkmenistan's Public Chamber Presidium Discusses State Policy and Development Strategies
item.description: The Presidium of the Halk Maslahaty (Public Chamber) of Turkmenistan convened to discuss the implementation of decisions from a previous session and national development strategies. Key topics included industrial development, education system improvements, youth policy, and the state protection of Akhal-Teke horses.

item.title: Turkmenistan Approves Schedule for Exhibitions, Fairs, Conferences, and Festivals in 2027
item.description: Turkmenistan's President has signed a decree approving the list of exhibitions, fairs, conferences, and festivals to be held in 2027. The decision aims to promote socio-economic reforms, expand international cooperation, and integrate modern technologies into production.

item.title: Turkmenistan Approves Composition of Turkmen Side of Intergovernmental Committee with Armenia
item.description: To implement bilateral agreements and further develop relations between Turkmenistan and the Republic of Armenia, the President of Turkmenistan has signed a decree. The decree officially approves the composition of the Turkmen side of the Intergovernmental Turkmen-Armenian Committee on Economic Cooperation.

item.title: UN Reports Over 6.5 Million Afghans Returned from Iran and Pakistan in Three Years
item.description: The United Nations reports that over 6.5 million Afghan citizens have returned from Iran and Pakistan in the past three years, with at least three million returning in 2025 alone. This significant influx has increased Afghanistan's population by about 10%, straining housing, job opportunities, and public services. The UNHCR has documented the difficulties faced by returnees who had established lives abroad.

item.title: Three Afghan Migrants Killed by Iranian Forces at Saravan Border, Rights Group Reports
item.description: The Halosh human rights organization reports that three Afghan citizens, including a woman and a child, were killed by Iranian military and border guards in the Saravan border area. Reports indicate the victims were shot in the head, and their bodies were subsequently covered with stones. Radio Azadi could not independently verify the report. This incident follows previous reports of deadly ambushes and direct shootings of migrant convoys by Iranian forces.

item.title: German AfD Co-Leader Calls for Deportation of 2.6 Million Foreign Nationals
item.description: Tino Chrupalla, co-leader of Germany's right-wing AfD party, has called for the deportation of up to 2.6 million foreign nationals. He stated that individuals from Ukraine, Syria, and Afghanistan should be returned if the conflicts in their home countries end or security improves. This comes after Germany deported 13 Afghan men to Kabul in September. The German Interior Ministry reports that 263 Afghan citizens have been deported since the current coalition government took office, mostly with criminal records.

item.title: Astana Police Intensify Checks, Deport 20 Foreign Nationals
item.description: Astana police have intensified patrols and checks on public places as part of the 'Legal Order' operation. Since the operation began, over 1200 administrative offenses have been identified. 97 cases related to migration law violations were filed, and 20 foreign citizens were forcibly expelled from Kazakhstan.

item.title: UN Climate Summit COP31 Fails to Agree on Final Document Over Fossil Fuels
item.description: The UN Climate Summit COP31 in Antalya concluded without an agreed final document due to disputes over fossil fuels. The EU and other nations refused to support an agreement that omitted a phase-out of oil, gas, and coal. Negotiations extended two days beyond the planned end date.

item.title: Student Develops Innovative Method for Producing Paving Stones from Waste
item.description: A student from Kyzylorda University has developed a technology to produce paving stones using ash from a thermal power plant and gravel from a Tasboget deposit. The goal is to reduce production costs and environmental impact by reusing industrial waste and local raw materials.

item.title: Tashkent Ranked 'Very High' in UN Local Online Services Index
item.description: Tashkent has climbed to 37th place globally in the UN's Local Online Service Index (LOSI), a significant jump from 95th. The city's index value increased from 0.3646 to 0.8911, moving it from 'medium' to 'very high' status, surpassing regional and global averages.

item.title: UNHCR: Over Six Million Afghans Returned Home in Three Years
item.description: The UNHCR reports that over 6.5 million Afghan nationals have returned to Afghanistan in the past three years, with nearly three million returning in 2025 alone. These returns have increased Afghanistan's population by over 10%, straining resources. Women and girls constitute over half of those under UNHCR protection and are in critical need of shelter and support.

item.title: Former Afghan Official Criticizes Germany's Taliban Policy as Double Standards
item.description: Rangin Dadfar Spanta, former Afghan national security adviser, has criticized Germany's policy towards the Taliban, calling it hypocritical and a double standard. He pointed to Germany allowing Taliban diplomats entry while Afghan doctors face restrictions in treating women. Spanta argued Western countries are disregarding democratic values and concealing their true objectives behind diplomatic language.

item.title: UN climate summit ends without agreement on fossil fuels
item.description: The UN climate summit (COP31) concluded without an agreement due to disagreements over phasing out fossil fuels. The European Union and other nations opposed a draft text prepared by Turkey and Australia, deeming it too weak to combat global warming.

item.title: Tashkent's Air Quality Expected to Deteriorate Tonight, Committee Warns
item.description: Uzbekistan's Ecology Committee has issued a warning that Tashkent's air quality may become 'unhealthy' between 8 PM and 11 PM on November 22. The situation is expected to improve after 2 AM. Residents are advised to be aware of the potential decline in air quality.

item.title: Elderly Man Dies by Suicide in Nangarhar Due to Poverty
item.description: An elderly man reportedly died by suicide by jumping from a hill in Achin District, Nangarhar province. Local sources stated that poverty and financial hardship were the reasons for his death. This incident occurs amidst reports of rising suicides linked to economic difficulties since the Taliban's return to power.

item.title: Taliban Allegedly Seek Bail for Man Accused of Murder in Farah
item.description: Local sources in Farah Province report that the Taliban are attempting to release Asadullah, accused of murdering Afsana, on bail. Asadullah, the victim's uncle-in-law, has a history of drug addiction and violence. His family is reportedly afraid to speak out due to his influence.

item.title: COP31 Climate Talks Collapse as EU and Others Reject Final Draft Deal
item.description: UN climate talks at COP31 collapsed Sunday after the European Union and other nations rejected the final draft agreement, deeming it too weak to combat global warming. The proposed deal had acknowledged projected temperature overshoot and called for faster development of carbon-removal technologies. Disagreements over fuels and climate finance were cited as dealbreakers.

item.title: Madrid Conference on Women’s Rights in Afghanistan Opens
item.description: The fourth HearUs Summit convened in Madrid on November 22-23, gathering Afghan women leaders, international officials, and human rights advocates. The conference, themed 'Afghan Women’s Leadership in Achieving Justice and Peace through Accountability,' aims to discuss women's role in Afghanistan's justice, accountability, and peace processes.

item.title: OIC Discusses Roadmap for Phased Engagement with Taliban Authorities
item.description: The Organization of Islamic Cooperation (OIC) has discussed a roadmap for phased engagement with Taliban authorities. This initiative aims to coordinate diplomatic dialogue and address Afghanistan's political, humanitarian, and economic challenges. A preparatory meeting in Jeddah reviewed a framework for structured communication with the Taliban, focusing on the evolving situation and potential staged engagement.
